English exercise: Alex asks WHO IS RUNNING over there? Bruce replies BEN AND HIS FRIENDS ARE. The general unknown-number subject-WHO question can be singular, even if its later answer names several people. If plural number is already known, plural WHO ARE RUNNING can be possible; never teach always singular. Alex is a teenage boy in a mustard hoodie, Bruce a different teenage boy in a blue jacket. Establish an ordinary question about people running now, no thought bubble, no past memory.
